rows.row: selection.extensions — user allowlist deliberately case-sensitive (README L170)
rows.note: caller must NOT reuse one preview result for both allowlists (different configs) — hence two separate runs
the lower tree additionally fails with the empty-scan-set violation (fail-closed), which is why its exit/passed value alone is not the discriminator — filesScanned is

rows.row: binary extension list already insensitive (README L168)
rows.note: both spellings are excluded with a binary reason ⇒ the list is case-insensitive

rows.row: policy.scanRoots: an unresolvable root ⇒ empty scan set = violation (README L173)
rows.docNuance: on this case-insensitive filesystem `SRC` resolves to `src` (filesScanned=1), so README L173’s "a case mismatch walks nothing" is only true on case-sensitive filesystems
